newsitem.title: USA: Jury deliberations delayed in Simpson trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury deliberations delayed in Simpson trial.

text.p: Jury deliberations in O.J. Simpson's civil trial were delayed on Friday as lawyers huddled with the judge behind closed doors and police investigated allegations of possible jury tampering.

The investigation was ordered by Judge Hiroshi Fujisaki after two of the civil trial jurors told him they had received a letter signed by two panellists from Simpson's criminal trial, in which he was acquitted in Oct. 1995 of the murders of his ex-wife and her friend.
The judge issued an order at the start of the civil trial prohibiting anyone from contacting jurors about the case.

Simpson is currently battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman, who were stabbed and slashed to death on June 12, 1994. Jurors began their deliberations on Tuesday after three months of testimony.

Deputies from the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department on Thursday night searched the home of Brenda Moran, one of the criminal court jurors who signed the letter, and carted away a computer, note pads and other documents.
Moran, who is writing a book on her experiences in the criminal trial, told reporters the letter was not supposed to have been mailed until the civil case was over.
"I wrote some of it, not all of it," she said. "The (agent) was supposed to give the (civil case) jurors this letter way after all of this was over with."
The letter, which was also signed by criminal case juror Gina Rosborough, urged the civil trial jurors to get in touch with their agent.

"Dear fellow jurors, congratulations on successfully surviving a trying experience ... We respect your verdict and look forward to meeting you and taking you to dinner or to a cup of coffee. You have a great opportunity to protect your rights and financial future by not talking to the press immediately," it said.
